about: What the land is made of under what covers it (the owner, 5 November, late: geology complements the hex geography, it does not compete with it): the formations a country's ground can be, each by the land covers it lies under and the region terrains it is found in, the rock it is (a material), the soil it makes, and the deposits it carries, each a material of data/catalog/materials.json with how often a cell of the formation holds it (in the fells and on the peaks, where it shows, more often). A generated country lays its formations in broad tracts and its deposits where they fall; settlements live by what they can dig, mines go where the ore is, and places are named for it.

granite.name: Granite
granite.looks: grey crags and tors, boulders strewn on the moor

slate.name: Slate country
slate.looks: blue-grey edges and scree, walls built of the same stone

ironstone.name: Ironstone
ironstone.looks: red-brown rock that stains the streams orange

limestone.name: Limestone
limestone.soil: sweet and thin, good for sheep
limestone.looks: pale scars and pavements, streams that go underground

sandstone.name: Sandstone
sandstone.looks: red and buff edges, soft rock that weathers into hollows

clay_vale.name: Clay vale
clay_vale.soil: heavy and wet, rich when it is drained
clay_vale.looks: low wet fields, sticky lanes, brick-red where it is dug

peat_moor.name: Peat moor
peat_moor.looks: black hags and bog-pools, cotton-grass blowing
